text: In 1885, a group of educated Indians founded the Indian National Congress.
At first, they just asked politely for more say.
In 1905, the British split Bengal in two.
Bengal exploded in protest.
People burned British cloth and bought Indian goods only.
Swadeshi.
In 1915, a lawyer came home from South Africa where he had spent 20 years fighting discrimination
against Indians.
He wore simple clothes and spoke softly.
His name was Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi.
People came to call him Mahatma, great soul.
His weapon was Satyagraha, holding on to the truth and resisting without violence.
fighting an empire without fighting? Let's see how this goes. In 1919, in Ummritsar,
thousands of people gathered peacefully in a walled garden called Jallian Walabag. A British
general, Reginald Dyer, blocked the only exit and ordered his troops to fire into the crowd.
They fired until they ran out of bullets. The official count said 379 dead. Indian estimates
were over a thousand. After Amritsar, millions of Indians who had trusted the
British stopped trusting them. Gandhi called on India to stop cooperating,
leave British schools, courts, and jobs, and burn foreign cloth. In 1930 he chose
an unlikely target, salt. The British taxed it and Indians were banned from
making their own. Mr. Gandhi, what exactly are you doing? Picking up salt? That's
illegal. Then arrest me and the thousands behind me. Looking at the crowd, I'll need
a bigger notebook.
